chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, who said:

I was present with Ibn Abī Laylā when he gave judgment concerning a man who had assigned the yield of his house to one of his relatives without setting a time limit. Then the man died, and his heirs came before Ibn Abī Laylā, and the relative for whom the yield of the house had been assigned was also present. So Ibn Abī Laylā said: “I think that I should leave it as its owner left it.”

Then Muḥammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafī said: “Indeed, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام had judged in this mosque contrary to what you have judged.” He said: “And what knowledge do you have of that?” He said: “I heard Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام saying:”
“ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled by returning the ḥabīs and carrying out the inheritances.”

So Ibn Abī Laylā said: “Do you have this in a book?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then send for it and bring it to me.” Muḥammad ibn Muslim said to him: “On the condition that you do not look in the book except at that hadith.” He said: “You have that.” He said: “So he brought the book and showed him the hadith from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام in the book, and he retracted his judgment.”

key_terms.الْحَبِيسِ: property restrained or assigned in a limited endowment-like arrangement
key_terms.الْكِتَابِ: the written record in which the hadith was preserved
key_terms.الْمَوَارِيثِ: the inheritances to be distributed among legal heirs
key_terms.غَلَّةَ: the yield or income produced from the property
key_terms.قَرَابَتِهِ: his relative or kin to whom the benefit was assigned
key_terms.قَضَى: he gave judgment or ruled judicially
key_terms.وَرَثَتُهُ: his heirs entitled to inheritance after his death

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام on a house yield granted to a relative without a time limit?
ai.summary: This hadith records a judicial dispute over the yield of a house granted to a relative without a specified term, and it preserves the ruling of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام that such a ḥabīs is to be returned and the rules of inheritance enforced. It also highlights the authority of the Imams عليهم السلام in legal knowledge and the use of recorded hadith to correct judicial decisions.
